messages.subject: RHadoop : Using custom input format
parts:
I already posted this question in stackoverflow, but later found this mailing list. So I am posting again here. Sorry for the redundant posts.

Here is my question
In my map reduce job, I have a requirement to process the whole file without splitting. So I have written a new input format to process the file as a whole by extending "org.apache.hadoop.mapred.FileInputFormat" and overriding the isSplittable() method. I have also created a new Record reader implementation to read the whole file and return the byte array. This works well in Java map reduce function. Now I want to use them in rHadoop.

So I created reader function as below. I used read.table as my file is CSV file. 

my.reader=function (con, keyval.length) 
{
df = tryCatch(read.table(file = con,header=F,
    colClasses=rep("numeric",9),sep=","), error = function(e) {
    if (e$message != "no lines available in input") 
        stop(e$message)
    NULL
})
#cbind(df)
if (is.null(df) || dim(df)[[1]] == 0) 
    NULL
else keyval(NULL, df)
}

Then created new RHadoop input format by specifying this function as reader and streaming.format as my fully qualified name of my whole file input format class.

my.input.format=make.input.format(mode = "binary", format = my.reader,streaming.format="WholeFileInputFormat")

I tried reading the CSV files in a sample HDFS folder using this new input format.

csv1=from.dfs(hdfs.data,format=my.input.format)

This folder contains 5 CSV files. I was expecting to see a list of 5 data frames each containing data from one CSV file. But I am getting a list of data frames corresponding to each column in my CSV file. Each data frame contains a specific column data of all CSV files. This means each file is not treated separately

Any idea what I am doing wrong here? Please help. Thanks.

messages.author: 6ac7e7dfbe4f6c38
messages.subject: Re: [RHadoop:#999] RHadoop : Using custom input format
parts:
Hi, 
off the bat the only problem I see here is the mode, which should be "text". I am not sure if that's going to make a huge difference, particularly on unix-like systems, but you are in uncharted territory, since the csv format uses a text connection. As far as your expectations, they are wrong, what you should get out of from.csv is a list of two elements, one NULL an one a data frame, the concatenation of the data frames returned by my.reader as second arg to keyval. What you are actually seeing defies both your and my expectations. Since you are just using from.dfs and not calling mapreduce, this should be relatively easy to debug. Unfortunately, for some reason debug(my.input.format$format) doesn't work. That's something for the R core members to fix so let's talk about workarounds. Modify my.reader with a browser() call. Try to read again. Inspect what you are getting from the connection (just do a  readLine and then start over again, as that will invalidate the rest of the parsing).  my.reader needs to return 
keyval(NULL, list(df)) 
or the data frames will be rbinded. Let me know what you find and I'll try to help. I hope your files are relatively small, otherwise the whole strategy is doomed. Maybe in the low GB it is still going to work. I would keep some system monitoring constantly on because you are pushing a little bit in the opposite direction of what the design was, which is read x records at a time, process, move on.

Antonio

I think before you spend more time down this road you should search for "Hadoop small file problem". There are many links, the classic is a Cloudera 2009 blog post but looking at this post http://amilaparanawithana.blogspot.com/2012/06/small-file-problem-in-hadoop.html it seems that as of 2012 the problem is still here. You need to look at the process that's creating the small files and change it. At least, that's what I would do from the limited information available.
